log.text: Floette used Light of Ruin → Rotom

decisions.rationale: Metagross is essential for Floette-Eternal: Mega Evolves and threatens with Tough Claws Meteor Mash while resisting Fairy. Klefki provides Prankster Reflect/Light Screen with Light Clay to neuter Garchomp and Talonflame, plus Thunder Wave speed control. Incineroar brings Fake Out pressure, Intimidate cycling, Flare Blitz for Floette/Goodra, and Parting Shot pivoting. Rotom-Wash is the Garchomp answer: Levitate avoids EQ, Will-O-Wisp cripples, Hydro Pump threatens. Dragapult left out due to Fairy weakness and Goodra wall; Corviknight redundant with Klefki's speed control and Rotom-Wash handling Talonflame.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Brought Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, Rotom-Wash. Opponent tendencies: Talonflame leads and sets Tailwind; Floette-Mega Protects turn 1; Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum; Goodra switches into special attackers. Plan: lead Klefki to set Reflect early; burn Garchomp on sight but scout Protects; preserve Metagross for Floette; use Parting Shot and Volt Switch to maintain momentum.

decisions.rationale: Lead Talonflame plus Garchomp for immediate Tailwind and Earthquake pressure while Talonflame is immune to Garchomp’s spread Ground damage. Floette-Eternal provides strong late-game special pressure into Incineroar and Rotom-Wash, while Milotic discourages Intimidate cycling and gives reliable speed control.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s game-2 four were Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash. Klefki showed Prankster Light Screen and Thunder Wave and likely has Reflect/Dazzling Gleam; deny or pressure it before screens compound. Incineroar repeatedly used Fake Out and Parting Shot with Intimidate and Sitrus Berry. Mega Metagross has Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect. Rotom-Wash can combine Volt Switch with Bullet Punch to pressure Talonflame. Dragapult and Corviknight were not brought in game 2.

decisions.rationale: Talonflame's Gale Wings Tailwind is inevitable and outspeeds Klefki's Prankster. Metagross Protects to dodge the likely Life Orb Earthquake (69–101% range, possible OHKO without Protect). Klefki sets Reflect at +1 priority after Tailwind but before Garchomp moves, halving EQ to ~33–48% on Klefki. Mega Evolving now gives Metagross better stats and Tough Claws for the rest of the game with no downside this turn. Reflect + Light Clay gives 8 turns of physical protection to handle Tailwind turns.

Rotom-Wash blanks Garchomp's STAB Ground moves with Levitate and resists Talonflame's Heat Wave, taking negligible damage under Reflect. It threatens both foes: Hydro Pump OHKO pressure on Garchomp, Volt Switch 2HKOs Talonflame through Sash. Incineroar's Intimidate doesn't offset the 50–70% it eats from Earthquake, leaving it too low to pivot effectively. Metagross stays in to preserve the Mega and threaten with priority Bullet Punch.
Apply immediate dual spread pressure: either screen only mitigates one attacking axis, while Earthquake is safe beside Talonflame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has again selected Mega Metagross and Klefki in game 3. Prioritize preventing Klefki from establishing prolonged dual-screen support; mixed special and physical pressure is effective into that pair.

decisions.rationale: Switch Metagross to Incineroar for Intimidate (-1 Atk on both foes), while Rotom Volt Switches into Talonflame for solid chip (45-88%) and pivots back to Metagross. Intimidate + Reflect neuters Garchomp's Earthquake on Incineroar to ~33-47%, and Talonflame's Tailwind is accepted but we gain board position: Incineroar (with Fake Out threat) + fresh Metagross vs weakened Talonflame and -1 Garchomp. This preserves Metagross for the likely Floette-Mega in back while cycling Intimidate.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Set Tailwind while Talonflame is still at full HP, then use Earthquake to pressure Mega Metagross without harming Talonflame or Rotom-Wash. Tailwind gives Garchomp and the remaining back line the best chance to control the next turns, including against a possible Dragapult.
decisions.notebook: Opponent again brought Mega Metagross and Klefki in game 3; Klefki established Reflect before fainting. Preserve mixed special and physical pressure into this core, and Tailwind is valuable for controlling potential Dragapult endgames.

decisions.rationale: Talonflame at 13% is very likely to Protect to dodge Bullet Punch, so Meteor Mash into Garchomp punishes that read while still dealing 41–74% if they attack instead. Parting Shot further cripples Garchomp to -2 Atk/-1 SpA and pivots Incineroar into Rotom-Wash, which is immune to Earthquake and resists Heat Wave. Even if Talonflame attacks, Metagross survives the combined Heat Wave + EQ, and Incineroar has a high chance to live both and execute the pivot.

Preserve the near-fainted Talonflame for a later Tailwind refresh, pivot Milotic into Incineroar's likely disruption, and Protect Garchomp from Fake Out or a Metagross double-target while retaining Tailwind initiative next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 opponent brought Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash. Klefki established Reflect and was removed. Incineroar revealed Intimidate, Fake Out, and Sitrus Berry; Rotom-Wash revealed Volt Switch; Mega Metagross has Bullet Punch and Protect. Preserve special pressure and Tailwind resources against Reflect-supported physical bulk.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar at 53% is guaranteed OHKO by Milotic Hydro Pump (66.3-101%) under Tailwind. Switching to Rotom-Wash saves it: Rotom is immune to Garchomp's Earthquake (Levitate) and resists Water/Ice, taking at most 35% from Hydro Pump. Metagross-Mega uses Protect at +4 priority to scout and avoid all damage; Protect resets to 100% success after non-consecutive use. This preserves all three Pokémon for the next turn when opponent Tailwind has only 1 turn left and Reflect still has 4 turns.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Brought Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, Rotom-Wash. Opponent tendencies: Talonflame leads and sets Tailwind; Floette-Mega Protects turn 1; Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum; Goodra switches into special attackers. Rotom-Wash walls Milotic and Garchomp's Ground moves with Levitate. Incineroar's Fake Out not yet used this switch-in cycle; preserve for Intimidate cycling and Fake Out pressure later.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind guarantees both attacks before normal-priority opposing moves; Hydro Pump is a guaranteed KO on the revealed Incineroar range, while Stomping Tantrum gives the same listed Metagross damage range as Earthquake without damaging Milotic.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 opponent’s four are Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash. Incineroar has Intimidate, Sitrus Berry, Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat; Mega Metagross has Tough Claws, Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect. Preserve special attackers when Reflect is active.

decisions.rationale: Double into Garchomp to remove it before Tailwind expires. Garchomp + Milotic both target Metagross for 64.3–96.2% combined (non-crit), which Metagross likely survives. Meteor Mash (40.9–73.8%) + Hydro Pump (27–48.1%) combine for 67.9–121.9% into 80% HP Garchomp — high probability KO. If Garchomp faints, only Milotic remains offensively and Tailwind ends, giving Metagross the speed advantage next turn. Hydro Pump miss (20%) is the main risk, but even then Metagross survives and we clean up next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Brought Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, Rotom-Wash. Opponent tendencies: Talonflame leads and sets Tailwind; Floette-Mega Protects turn 1; Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum; Goodra switches into special attackers. Rotom-Wash walls Milotic and Garchomp's Ground moves with Levitate. Incineroar's Fake Out not yet used this switch-in cycle; preserve for Intimidate cycling and Fake Out pressure later. Avoid switching Incineroar into Milotic due to Competitive.

decisions.rationale: Icy Wind preserves speed control after Tailwind ends while Stomping Tantrum is powered up from the blocked prior attempt and pressures Mega Metagross through Reflect.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Game 3 roster is Mega Metagross, Klefki, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash. Incineroar is Intimidate/Sitrus with Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat. Mega Metagross is Jolly Tough Claws with Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect. Prioritize special damage while Reflect is up and maintain speed control into Mega Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Bring in the healthy Floette-Eternal; Talonflame is guaranteed to fall to Bullet Punch from its current HP, while Floette preserves a meaningful Mega Evolution and Energy Ball win condition against Rotom-Wash.

Bullet Punch (priority +1) always strikes before Floette can act, and Hydro Pump adds insurance. Combined into base Floette the minimum roll is 104.5 %; even after Mega Evolution the two hits together KO across the vast majority of the range. If Floette Protects both moves are blocked, but Metagross cannot reasonably Protect itself (1/9 success after two prior uses) and Rotom must not Volt Switch into Incineroar while Milotic is present (Competitive boosts + Sitrus-proof Hydro Pump OHKO Incineroar through Reflect). Any line that leaves Metagross in risks the speed tie with Milotic; Bullet Punch at least guarantees Metagross gets its attack off.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Light of Ruin -> foe 1 (Rotom-Wash) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Apply simultaneous KO pressure: Mega Light of Ruin threatens Rotom-Wash while Hydro Pump threatens Mega Metagross, making a single Protect unable to cover both.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette is Fairy Aura with higher offensive stats and Speed; Mega Metagross is Jolly Tough Claws with Bullet Punch, Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, and Protect. Incineroar is Intimidate/Sitrus with Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat. Prioritize special offense through Reflect and use dual-target pressure to punish Protect.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Fake Out Milotic (priority +3) flinches it, preventing Hydro Pump. Bullet Punch (priority +1) KOs 13% Talonflame before it moves — Focus Sash only activates at full HP. This line is resilient to opponent Protect: if Talonflame Protects (+4 blocks Bullet Punch), Milotic is still flinched and Metagross survives; next turn Talonflame's Protect is unreliable and Bullet Punch KOs. The alternative Fake Out Talonflame + Zen Headbutt Milotic line has ~45% win rate (90% acc × ~50% OHKO roll) and folds completely if Talonflame Protects. After turn 7 this line yields a 2v1 vs +2 Milotic; turn 8 will require both mons attacking Milotic (Zen Headbutt + Darkest Lariat) hoping for favorable speed tie and damage rolls.

Protect Talonflame from the immediate Fake Out/Bullet Punch pressure while Milotic threatens a guaranteed Hydro Pump KO on Incineroar; if Fake Out stops Milotic, Talonflame is still preserved for the following turn after Fake Out is spent.
decisions.notebook: Incineroar has Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, and Darkest Lariat with Intimidate and Sitrus Berry. Mega Metagross is Jolly Tough Claws with Bullet Punch, Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, and Protect. Milotic's Competitive punishes Intimidate sharply; prioritize its special Water damage into Incineroar and use Talonflame Protect to absorb priority pressure when needed.

decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch (+1 priority) guarantees KO on 13% Talonflame before it acts, removing one threat. Darkest Lariat into Milotic (30–57%) is stronger than Flare Blitz (21–40%, NVE). The hard truth: Milotic outspeeds Incineroar and +2 Hydro Pump OHKOs it (133–200%); if Hydro Pump hits, Incineroar faints before Darkest Lariat lands. Our only realistic win condition is the 20% Hydro Pump miss — then Darkest Lariat lands, and turn 9 becomes 2v1 Metagross+Incineroar vs damaged Milotic. No other line offers a better chance.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Series tied 1-1. Opponent tendencies: Talonflame leads and sets Tailwind; Floette-Mega Protects turn 1; Garchomp spams Stomping Tantrum; Goodra switches into special attackers. Rotom-Wash walls Milotic and Garchomp's Ground moves with Levitate. Incineroar's Fake Out pressure and Intimidate cycling are valuable; avoid switching Incineroar into Milotic due to Competitive.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Remove Incineroar with Milotic’s boosted Hydro Pump; Talonflame’s reduced-success Protect is still its only chance to avoid Mega Metagross’s Bullet Punch and preserve support for the endgame.
decisions.notebook: Incineroar is Adamant Intimidate with Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Parting Shot, Darkest Lariat, and Sitrus Berry. Mega Metagross is Jolly Tough Claws with Bullet Punch, Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, and Protect. Milotic’s Competitive reliably punishes Intimidate; prioritize its boosted special Water damage into Incineroar while using Talonflame Protect when priority pressure is likely.

decisions.rationale: Only Metagross-Mega remains at 4% HP vs Milotic 89%. Any Milotic attack KOs. Bullet Punch and Meteor Mash cannot KO even with max rolls. Zen Headbutt has a chance to KO (59.4-111.2%, need ≥89% to avoid Sitrus Berry activation) and shares the same 90% accuracy as Meteor Mash. Speed order is uncertain (118 vs 101-133), but Zen Headbutt is the only path to victory. Incineroar is fainted; Pass is the only non-concession option.
Ice Beam is perfectly accurate and guarantees the KO on the revealed 3% Mega Metagross.
decisions.notebook: Mega Metagross is Jolly Tough Claws with Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect; respect Bullet Punch priority when preserving frail Pokémon.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar is fainted so must pass. Metagross-Mega at 4% HP faces Milotic at 39%. Bullet Punch (priority +1) goes first but deals only 14.9–28.2%, cannot KO, and Milotic KOs back. Meteor Mash (33.2–62.4%) might KO but is not guaranteed. Zen Headbutt (59.4–111.2%) guarantees the KO on hit. Speed order is uncertain (Metagross 118 vs Milotic 101–133), but Zen Headbutt is the only move that wins if Metagross is faster. Protect only delays the inevitable. Zen Headbutt maximizes win probability.
Ice Beam is accurate and easily finishes the 3% Mega Metagross if Milotic gets to act.

reflections.summary: We won the series 2-1 by adapting our leads to the opponent's predictable Talonflame + Garchomp opening. In Game 3, bringing Klefki for screens backfired slightly as it fainted early, but Reflect still provided durability. Metagross's priority and a clutch Zen Headbutt flinch on a Competitive-boosted Milotic secured a narrow win after Floette-Mega self-destructed. The opponent's over-reliance on Talonflame/Garchomp and failure to manage the Milotic vs. Metagross endgame cost them the game.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a future series, lead Incineroar + Rotom-Wash to Fake Out Talonflame and threaten Garchomp with Hydro Pump or Will-O-Wisp. Rotom’s Volt Switch can pivot into Metagross or Dragapult to maintain pressure. Consider replacing Klefki with a bulkier support like Corviknight that handles Garchomp and Floette, or bring Dragapult to outspeed and KO Talonflame before Tailwind. Prioritize removing Talonflame early to deny speed control, and be extremely careful about triggering Milotic’s Competitive with Intimidate.
reflections.notebook: Opponent reliably leads Talonflame + Garchomp: Talonflame sets Tailwind or uses Heat Wave, Garchomp clicks Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum. Stomping Tantrum’s power doubles after a failed move (e.g., our Protect), so avoid giving it a free boost. Floette-Mega packs Light of Ruin with massive recoil that can knock itself out; it often Protects on its first turn in. Milotic carries Sitrus Berry and Competitive—Intimidate triggers a +2 Special Attack, making it a major late-game threat. Goodra-Hisui has Sap Sipper and special bulk, but stayed on the bench. Scrafty adds secondary Intimidate and Fake Out, so expect Fake Out pressure if they bring it. Rotom-Wash is our best answer to Garchomp and Milotic thanks to Levitate and resistances; Will-O-Wisp neutralizes physical attackers. Klefki’s screens are valuable but it must be positioned safely (e.g., behind Fake Out). Priority moves like Metagross’s Bullet Punch are crucial for cleaning weakened threats. In team preview, assume the Talonflame/Garchomp core; tailor leads to eliminate Talonflame quickly and limit Stomping Tantrum’s potential.

reflections.summary: The deciding Game 3 was lost because the early Klefki removal and later Rotom knockout did not translate into a clean answer to Mega Metagross. Reflect reduced the pressure on Metagross, Garchomp fell before finishing it, and Mega Floette had to trade itself through Light of Ruin after Bullet Punch left it frail. Milotic then missed its chance to remove the remaining Metagross, leaving the opponent's Mega at minimal health; Fake Out and two recorded Zen Headbutt flinches prevented Milotic from recovering the endgame. Piloting was not the issue: the record lists zero decision errors or defaults. The Game 3 plan had real successes, but it ultimately backfired by allowing Mega Metagross to remain alive long enough to use Bullet Punch and close the game, which clinched the 1-2 series loss. The Talonflame/Garchomp/Milotic/Floette bring was broadly sensible into Klefki, Incineroar, Rotom-Wash, and Metagross, and Mega Floette was the only registered Mega option; however, its Bullet Punch vulnerability and Light of Ruin recoil made it a poor long-term endgame piece against this board. The supplied evidence does not establish what specific between-game adjustments were made, nor does it show that unbrought Scrafty or Hisuian Goodra offered a materially superior alternative.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, build the game plan around securing a reliable Mega Metagross knockout before committing Mega Floette to a recoil trade or leaving Talonflame in Bullet Punch range. Continue exploiting the Talonflame plus Garchomp Earthquake pairing to pressure Klefki and Metagross, but account for Rotom-Wash's Ground immunity and Klefki's screen support. Preserve Milotic's ability to act after Incineroar enters: Competitive is valuable against Intimidate, but the opponent demonstrated Fake Out pressure that can deny the key attack. Do not assume that a nearly defeated Mega Metagross is harmless; keep a non-flinched, non-priority-vulnerable route to finish it. Preparation-wise, the registered core had useful tools for this matchup, while there is insufficient supplied evidence about Scrafty's or Hisuian Goodra's sets to claim they were clearly better selections.
reflections.notebook: Opponent revealed Mega Metagross with Meteor Mash, Zen Headbutt, Bullet Punch, and Protect; it is Jolly and should be respected as a priority endgame cleaner, especially against Mega Floette and weakened Talonflame. Klefki is Prankster Light Clay dual screens with Thunder Wave and Dazzling Gleam; immediate pressure can remove it, but Reflect can still materially protect Metagross. Incineroar is Adamant Sitrus with Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz, and Darkest Lariat; Milotic's Competitive punishes its Intimidate, but Fake Out can deny Milotic's key turn. Rotom-Wash is Bold Leftovers with Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect, and invalidates Ground targeting through Levitate. In Game 3 the opponent chose Metagross/Klefki with Incineroar and Rotom-Wash, leaving Dragapult and Corviknight out; treat that as a revealed game-specific composition, not a guaranteed future tendency. Prep priority: maintain a dependable Metagross-finishing line after screens and prioritize preserving anti-Bullet-Punch resources.
